findings.title: limitFunction drops all caller arguments
findings.cause: The returned wrapper is `() => limit(() => function_())`, so it ignores the arguments passed to the limited function instead of forwarding `...arguments_`.
findings.impact: Any wrapped function that depends on parameters receives no arguments at runtime, while the TypeScript declaration still advertises `(...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>`.
findings.evidence: index.js:121-124 returns a zero-argument wrapper. index.d.ts:133-136 declares that the returned function accepts and forwards the original argument tuple.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused probe: `const f = limitFunction(async (...args) => args, {concurrency: 1}); await f('alpha', 'beta')` printed `[]`.

findings.title: limit.map omits indexes for non-array iterables
findings.cause: The implementation passes `index` only when `Array.isArray(iterable)` is true and passes `undefined` for Sets, iterators, strings, Maps, and other iterable inputs.
findings.impact: The documented iterable contract is broken for non-array iterables: mappers that use the index receive `undefined` despite the public API promising an item index.
findings.evidence: index.js:107-112 gates the index on `Array.isArray`. readme.md:78-84 and index.d.ts:30-43 say the mapper receives the item value and its index and is equivalent to `Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => limit(mapperFunction, item, index))`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused probe: `await limit.map(new Set(['a', 'b']), (value, index) => ({value, indexType: typeof index}))` printed `indexType:"undefined"` for both entries.

findings.title: Options-object clearQueue rejects pending promises by default
findings.cause: When the options-object form is used, destructuring defaults `rejectOnClear` to `true` instead of the documented default `false`.
findings.impact: Existing callers using `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` can get unexpected `AbortError` rejections from pending tasks when `clearQueue()` is called, including unexpected `Promise.all` rejection paths.
findings.evidence: index.js:6-8 defaults `rejectOnClear = true`. readme.md:46-52 and index.d.ts:99-106 document `rejectOnClear` as optional with default `false`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused probe queued one running task and one pending task with `pLimit({concurrency: 1})`, called `clearQueue()`, and the pending promise status printed `rejected:AbortError` instead of remaining pending/discarded.

findings.title: Falsey non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass validation
findings.cause: The runtime type check is guarded by `if (rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean')`, so invalid falsey values skip validation.
findings.impact: Invalid option values such as `0`, an empty string, `null`, or `NaN` are silently accepted even though the public option type is boolean.
findings.evidence: index.js:12-14 only rejects truthy non-boolean values. readme.md:46-49 and index.d.ts:99-106 define `rejectOnClear` as a boolean option.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused probe tried `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0})`, `''`, and `null`; all were accepted without throwing.

findings.title: Infinity concurrency is rejected
findings.cause: The concurrency validator now requires `Number.isInteger(concurrency)`, removing the existing `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` allowance.
findings.impact: Callers that use `Infinity` as an explicit unbounded concurrency limit now get a `TypeError`, even though the previous implementation accepted it and the public type is a number with only a minimum bound.
findings.evidence: index.js:127-130 rejects non-integers. `git show HEAD:index.js` showed the prior validator accepted `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`; readme.md:37-44 and index.d.ts:91-97 state a number minimum of 1 with no upper bound.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Focused probe: `pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)` printed `infinity rejected: TypeError Expected \`concurrency\` to be a number from 1 and up`.
